source.trial: Fixed-effect pool of CIBIS-II (bisoprolol), MERIT-HF (metoprolol CR/XL), COPERNICUS (carvedilol)

population: LVEF <=35 (CIBIS-II), <=40 (MERIT-HF), <25 (COPERNICUS); NYHA II-IV overall (CIBIS-II III-IV), on ACEi/diuretic; all rhythms

source.trial: Cleland 2018 Table 2 (atrial fibrillation, LVEF below 40%, cardiovascular hospitalization), converted to heart failure hospitalization
source.citation: Cleland JGF et al. Eur Heart J 2018;39:26-35 (Table 2, open-access full text)

Conversion: HF hospitalization HR = (cardiovascular hospitalization HR) ^ k, with k = ln(0.64) / ln(0.768) = 1.693, where 0.64 is the CIBIS-II heart failure hospitalization figure (quoted second-hand) and 0.768 (0.716 to 0.824) is the pool of the four sinus-rhythm cardiovascular hospitalization strata below 40% in the same table. Converted value 0.847 (0.657 to 1.093); the interval carries the sampling error of the pooled figure and the uncertainty of k (from the intervals of 0.64 and of 0.768). The assumption that heart failure admissions scale with cardiovascular admissions in the same way as in sinus rhythm is untested.
notes: Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review): added so that hospitalization, like death, is conditioned on the current rhythm; before this the sinus-rhythm benefit was applied to patients in atrial fibrillation. population: Sinus rhythm, LVEF 40-49%, n=566 (CV hospitalization)

extrapolation: Reduced band: pool of the four sinus-rhythm strata below 40% for cardiovascular hospitalization (<20: 0.70 (0.60-0.81); 20-25: 0.75 (0.66-0.85); 26-34: 0.84 (0.74-0.94); 35-39: 0.75 (0.61-0.91)), inverse-variance on the log scale = 0.768 (0.716-0.824). source.trial: Cleland 2018 IPD (LVEF >=50, sinus rhythm) vs Zheng 2018 and Cochrane 2021 (LVEF >40/>=40) meta-analyses
source.citation: Cleland JGF et al. Eur Heart J 2018;39:26-35; Zheng SL et al. Heart 2018;104:407-15; Martin N et al. Cochrane 2021;CD012721

population: Sinus rhythm LVEF >=50 (n=241 analysed) and trials with LVEF >=40/>40 (SENIORS subgroup EF >35%, J-DHF, small RCTs)
quote: Cleland Table 2, sinus rhythm, LVEF >=50%: 24/241 events, all-cause mortality HR 1.79 (0.78-4.10); P = 0.17. Zheng 2018: All-cause mortality was reduced with beta-blocker therapy compared with placebo (RR: 0.78, 95%CI 0.65 to 0.94, p=0.008). Cochrane 2021: There may be little to no effect on all-cause mortality (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.00; 1105 participants; four studies; low-certainty evidence).
extrapolation: Randomized evidence conflicts in direction, so no effect is assumed and NO INTERVAL is shown. The preference order would put the pooled randomized figure first: Cochrane 2021 (34022072), all-cause mortality RR 0.82 (95% CI 0.67 to 1.00), 1,105 participants, four studies, low-certainty evidence (and Zheng 2018, RR 0.78, 0.65 to 0.94). But the only band-specific patient-level figures, Cleland 2018 Table 2 (PMC5837435), point the other way in sinus rhythm: LVEF 50 or more, 24/241 events, HR 1.79 (0.78-4.10), P = 0.17 (in atrial fibrillation 8/73, HR 0.86 (0.19-3.94)). The pools are driven by SENIORS (LVEF above 35%, HR 0.92 (0.61-1.36)) and open-label J-DHF, which cover LVEF 36-49 as much as 50 or more. The two sources conflict in direction, so the row is the conflicting-evidence basis at 1.0 (controller ruling 2026-11-19, round 1 review, E9).
conflict_summary: Randomized evidence conflicts, so no effect is assumed and no interval is shown. Pooled trials above LVEF 40 point to fewer deaths (Cochrane 2021, risk ratio 0.82, 0.67 to 1.00; Zheng 2018, 0.78, 0.65 to 0.94), but they are driven by SENIORS and the open-label J-DHF, which cover LVEF 36 to 49 as much as 50 or more. The only patient-level figure for LVEF 50 or more (Cleland 2018) points the other way in sinus rhythm: hazard ratio 1.79 (0.78 to 4.10), 24 of 241 events; in atrial fibrillation 0.86 (0.19 to 3.94).
notes: The earlier displayed interval 0.65 to 4.10 was the envelope of the lowest and highest quoted limits (Zheng lower, Cleland upper); it is not a confidence interval of any estimate and is no longer stored or shown. Cleland's interval and Cochrane's both include 1; Zheng's does not. Alternative reading: Zheng/Cochrane would give 0.78-0.82.

source.trial: CLOROTIC (HCTZ added to IV furosemide)
source.citation: Trullas JC, et al. Eur Heart J 2023;44:411-21; EF split JACC Heart Fail 2024;12:1719-30 (PMID 38934966)

population: Acute HF inpatients (median LVEF 55%), n=230; no chronic outcome trial
quote: There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations.
extrapolation: No outcome evidence: CLOROTIC (hydrochlorothiazide added to intravenous furosemide, 230 acute-HF inpatients, median LVEF 55%, 64 with LVEF 40 or below) found "no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations", which at that size is uninformative, not evidence of no effect; no chronic outcome trial exists; no effect is assumed (rr 1.0, no interval).
notes: EVIDENCE: CLOROTIC (230 acute-HF inpatients, median LVEF 55%, 72% LVEF >40%; HCTZ vs placebo added to IV furosemide for 4 days): 'There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations'; the EF-split paper: 'no significant differences observed with the addition of HCTZ in terms of mortality, rehospitalizations, or safety endpoints ... among the 2 LVEF groups'. No hazard ratios are in any abstract, so none is entered. HCTZ added weight loss (2.3 vs 1.5 kg) but more renal-function worsening (46.5% vs 17.2%). This is an acute diuretic-response trial, not a chronic outcome trial; metolazone and chlorthalidone have no HF outcome RCT that I found, so CLOROTIC is applied to all three. OWNER DECISION: neutral (1.0).

source.trial: DIAMOND (patiromer); REALIZE-K (SZC)
source.citation: Butler J, et al. Eur Heart J 2022;43:4362-73; Kosiborod MN, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol 2025;85:971-84

population: HFrEF with hyperkalemia on RAAS inhibitors (DIAMOND n=878 randomized; REALIZE-K n=203); no outcome trial
quote: CONCLUSION: Concurrent use of patiromer and high-dose MRAs reduces the risk of recurrent hyperkalemia (DIAMOND, PMID 35900838): potassium and MRA dose were the endpoints; the abstract reports no clinical-event result.
extrapolation: No outcome evidence: DIAMOND (patiromer) measured potassium and MRA dose, not events, and had its primary endpoint revised from cardiovascular death or hospitalization to change in potassium; no effect is assumed (rr 1.0, no interval). Benefit, if any, is indirect, by allowing a RAAS inhibitor or MRA to continue, and is not credited here.
notes: Both binders: no outcome trial of death or hospitalization. See the sodium zirconium cyclosilicate hospitalization rows for the REALIZE-K signal. DIAMOND (patiromer, HFrEF with RAASi-related hyperkalemia, 439 vs 439 randomized, median 27 weeks): its primary endpoint was REVISED from time to CV death/CV hospitalization to change in potassium (full text: 'the primary endpoint was revised during the study from time to first occurrence of cardiovascular death or cardiovascular hospitalization, to changes in serum potassium levels'); no clinical-event HR was reported. Effects were on potassium (HR 0.63 for K >5.5) and MRA dose reduction (HR 0.62), so any benefit is indirect, via enabling RAAS inhibitor/MRA.

source.trial: REALIZE-K (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate), exploratory composite
source.citation: Kosiborod MN, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol 2025;85:971-84

caveats: REALIZE-K was a randomized-withdrawal trial: patients who had their potassium controlled on the binder were randomized to continue it or to switch to placebo. The figure is the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure (hospitalizations and urgent visits), an exploratory endpoint with 14 events (11 of 102 patients on the binder against 3 of 101 on placebo; nominal P 0.034).

It is converted here to heart failure hospitalization and carried to this EF band. It points toward harm from the binder, but it is a possible signal, not an established finding, and the trial was not designed to test it.
population: HFrEF (LVEF 40% or less) with hyperkalemia on spironolactone, 203 randomized (102 sodium zirconium cyclosilicate, 101 placebo), 6 months after randomized withdrawal; carried to other EF bands
comparator: placebo (after randomized withdrawal of the binder)
quote: Exploratory endpoints included a composite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure (HF) events (hospitalizations and urgent visits). ... Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death or worsening HF occurred in 11 (11%) participants in the SZC group (1 with CV death, 10 with HF events) and 3 (3%) participants in the placebo group (1 with CV death, 2 with HF events; log-rank nominal P = 0.034). ... Although underpowered for clinical outcomes, more participants had HF events with SZC than placebo, which should be factored into the clinical decision making.
extrapolation: Extrapolated, and a possible HARM signal: the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure events (hospitalizations and urgent visits) from a randomized-withdrawal trial, an EXPLORATORY endpoint on 14 events, applied to heart failure hospitalization. Crude risk ratio (11/102) / (3/101) = 3.63; interval from the log standard error sqrt(1/11 - 1/102 + 1/3 - 1/101) = 0.636: 1.04 to 12.63. The interval is wide and the precision weighting pulls the value strongly toward no effect.
notes: Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review) (E8): replaces "assumed neutral" for sodium zirconium cyclosilicate, which ignored this signal. The authors write that more participants had HF events with the binder than with placebo and that this should be factored into clinical decisions. Randomized-withdrawal design (everyone took the binder in the run-in), so it is not a standard randomized comparison of the drug against none. Patiromer has no clinical-event result and stays at no outcome evidence.

source.trial: REALIZE-K (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate), exploratory composite
source.citation: Kosiborod MN, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol 2025;85:971-84

caveats: REALIZE-K was a randomized-withdrawal trial: patients who had their potassium controlled on the binder were randomized to continue it or to switch to placebo. The figure is the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure (hospitalizations and urgent visits), an exploratory endpoint with 14 events (11 of 102 patients on the binder against 3 of 101 on placebo; nominal P 0.034).

It is converted here to heart failure hospitalization and carried to this EF band. It points toward harm from the binder, but it is a possible signal, not an established finding, and the trial was not designed to test it.
population: HFrEF (LVEF 40% or less) with hyperkalemia on spironolactone, 203 randomized (102 vs 101), 6 months; carried to preserved EF
comparator: placebo (after randomized withdrawal of the binder)
quote: Exploratory endpoints included a composite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure (HF) events (hospitalizations and urgent visits). ... Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death or worsening HF occurred in 11 (11%) participants in the SZC group (1 with CV death, 10 with HF events) and 3 (3%) participants in the placebo group (1 with CV death, 2 with HF events; log-rank nominal P = 0.034). ... Although underpowered for clinical outcomes, more participants had HF events with SZC than placebo, which should be factored into the clinical decision making.
extrapolation: Extrapolated, and a possible HARM signal: the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure events (hospitalizations and urgent visits) from a randomized-withdrawal trial, an EXPLORATORY endpoint on 14 events, applied to heart failure hospitalization. Crude risk ratio (11/102) / (3/101) = 3.63; interval from the log standard error sqrt(1/11 - 1/102 + 1/3 - 1/101) = 0.636: 1.04 to 12.63. The interval is wide and the precision weighting pulls the value strongly toward no effect.
notes: Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review) (E8): replaces "assumed neutral" for sodium zirconium cyclosilicate, which ignored this signal. The authors write that more participants had HF events with the binder than with placebo and that this should be factored into clinical decisions. Randomized-withdrawal design (everyone took the binder in the run-in), so it is not a standard randomized comparison of the drug against none. Patiromer has no clinical-event result and stays at no outcome evidence.
